transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-10 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48 min | Attendees: Jared Lee; Priya Shah; Marta Nguyen; Marcus Grant; Sofia Ramos; Liam O'Hara; Ana Perez

Summary: Short discovery on Private VPC deployment options for Redwood Private. Customer wants clarification on network connectivity (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region availability, egress controls, KMS integration, and audit/logging. Discussed dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs and next steps for pilot.

Topics: 1) Network connectivity options (VPC peering, PrivateLink/Private Service Connect, peering limits) 2) Private endpoints & IP allowlist 3) Egress/NAT and outbound internet requirements 4) KMS / key management and encryption at rest 5) Compliance/SOC2 and audit logs 6) Pilot timeline and success criteria

[00:00] Jared Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'll let priya give a short run on how we typically do private deployments, then we'll get into your network constraints.
[00:18] Priya Shah: thanks jared. hi all, priya from redwood infra. for private / vpc we have a couple common patterns: VPC peering (cross-account peering), cloud private endpoints like AWS PrivateLink or GCP Private Service Connect, and for on-prem or direct connects we can also do transit gateway or private link to your data center. Each has tradeoffs on route table complexity and egress.
[00:39] Marcus Grant: cool. our main ask is that data never traverse the public internet. we want model inference inside our vpc or via private connectivity. also region constraints — we need eu-west-1 for residency. is that supported for private?
[00:58] Priya Shah: yes we have private deployments in eu-west-1 via our private control plane offering. there are two flavors: customer-managed VPC where you host nodes in your subnets, or Redwood-managed private deployment where we run nodes in a dedicated VPC that peers to yours. both keep traffic off the public internet when configured with PrivateLink or peering.
[01:20] Sofia Ramos: i'm trying to understand the difference operationally — with peering do we have to manage route tables and nat gateways? what about egress to S3 for model artifacts?
[01:35] Priya Shah: good question. with VPC peering you will need route table entries for the peered CIDRs. egress to S3 can be done via VPC endpoints (S3 gateway endpoints) or through a proxy/ NAT depending on your setup. with PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) the endpoint is an ENI in your subnet and you don't need route table changes beyond the endpoint, but you do need an interface endpoint and security group rules to allow traffic. private link hides the provider VPC behind the endpoint interface.
[02:03] Liam O'Hara: what about limits — peering has aws limits on number of peering connections and cross-account stuff. we have multiple accounts. can you support transit gateway?
[02:15] Priya Shah: yes we commonly integrate with transit gateway for multi-account setups. Redwood's dedicated/private stack can attach to a transit gateway or be behind a PrivateLink front door. for very large enterprise setups we recommend transit gateway for scale and simplified routing.
[02:28] Marcus Grant: and latency? our real-time assistants need sub-200ms p95 within europe. if the model is running in your managed vpc but in the same region what kind of network latency can we expect?
[02:41] Priya Shah: network-wise if everything is in-region and a single hop via PrivateLink or peering we typically see under 10-20ms internal networking latency. model inference latency depends more on the model size and reserved capacity. dedicated GPU pools help there. we can run benchmarks with your payload to get realistic p95 numbers.
[03:03] Jared Lee: to add, for latency-sensitive workloads customers often pick Dedicated with pinned capacity in eu-west-1. we offer reserved capacity so you get predictable throughput.
[03:11] Ana Perez: KMS and key management: can we bring our own keys? we need HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest.
[03:19] Priya Shah: yes, for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, CloudHSM integrations). Redwood's control plane can be configured to use your keys for disk encryption and for model artifact encryption. we'll need to walk through IAM roles and key policies so the service principal has decrypt/encrypt permissions.
[03:40] Sofia Ramos: audit logs — we need all inference requests logged to our SIEM, redact PII, and retain logs for 1 year. is flow logs enough?
[03:50] Marta Nguyen: our offering includes audit/event logs from the control plane and per-request traces you can ingest. we can forward logs to your S3/GCS or push via Kinesis/Cloud Pub/Sub. note we also have structured trace IDs so you can correlate requests, but actual payload logging and PII redaction you'd control — we have hooks for excluding user content or transforming before export.
[04:15] Marcus Grant: ok good. can you tell me about IP addressing? we prefer to control all IPs in our address space. how does Redwood handle IPs for private endpoints?
[04:26] Priya Shah: with interface endpoints (PrivateLink) the ENI gets an IP from your subnet — so you control the address. with peering we don't allocate IPs into your space, it's routing rules only. For Redwood-managed VPC we provide a peering or endpoint and we can also support bringing your subnets via shared services or hosted connections depending on cloud provider.
[04:50] Liam O'Hara: egress firewall rules — do we need to open port ranges to your control plane? we run strict egress allowlist only to specific IPs and ports.
[04:59] Priya Shah: for PrivateLink you just open to the interface endpoint private IPs and SGs; for peering you allow the peered CIDRs. if you're using a Redwood-managed control plane in the same region there may be a small set of control-plane IPs for health checks and metrics; we'll provide a list and can rotate keys if needed. we also support mutual TLS mTLS for service-to-service authentication.
[05:24] Marcus Grant: cloud provider specifics — we are on AWS primarily. what about GCP/Azure customers?
[05:31] Priya Shah: patterns are similar across clouds but names differ: AWS PrivateLink / Interface Endpoint, GCP Private Service Connect, Azure Private Endpoint. transit gateway equivalents differ (TGW, Cloud VPN + Interconnect), but Redwood supports deployments in multiple clouds; the connectivity patterns are analogous.
[05:50] Sofia Ramos: region constraints — we need residency in eu-west-1 and can't route across regions. can you promise we won't spill to other regions for inference?
[05:59] Priya Shah: yes, we can lock workloads to region-specific capacity and pin to specific clusters. if you choose Redwood-managed dedicated in eu-west-1 we won't route traffic out of region. for hosted API there is some global routing unless you use our dedicated/private option.
[06:22] Ana Perez: for compliance we also need SSO/SAML integration and RBAC — can Redwood integrate with Okta?
[06:29] Marta Nguyen: yep, we integrate with SAML SSO providers (Okta, Azure AD). RBAC can be mapped from your groups and we support audit trails per user.
[06:39] Marcus Grant: pricing quick question — is there extra cost for PrivateLink / peering vs hosted?
[06:45] Jared Lee: there can be some infra costs — interface endpoints have per-hour charges on AWS and data processing charges. Our Private offering has a platform fee + reserved capacity pricing. we'll send a small spreadsheet with sample TCO for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[07:00] Sofia Ramos: curious about certificate management — how do we rotate certs and trust between our VPC and your nodes?
[07:07] Priya Shah: we support automations for certificate rotation and mTLS. we can accept your CA bundle or manage certs for you. for PrivateLink the interface endpoint trusts are handled by AWS; for peering it's all within your routing so standard TLS mTLS flows apply.
[07:25] Liam O'Hara: to be nitpicky, what about ephemeral IPs for burst nodes? if you autoscale do new nodes show up from your side and do we need to open more CIDRs?
[07:35] Priya Shah: for Redwood-managed autoscaling, we use a fixed set of CIDRs per deployment — we can provide an allowlist range that's large enough to cover bursts; you don't need to change rules per node. for customer-managed nodes (i.e., you host GPUs in your VPC) you control the IPs entirely.
[07:55] Marcus Grant: how is data persisted? do you store model logs or prompts on your side?
[08:02] Marta Nguyen: logs and telemetry are stored in the control plane; for private deployments we can configure retention and export. for a strict data residency policy we can disable persistent storage of request payloads or route logs to your storage immediately.
[08:19] Ana Perez: about onboarding - what's a realistic pilot? we want to test POC with a small set of 3 models and up to 5k requests/day.
[08:28] Jared Lee: that's a pretty normal pilot. we typically do a 2-4 week POC with a dedicated capacity slice or host it in your VPC with a small node pool. we'll run a baseline benchmark and KPIs: latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, and error rate.
[08:45] Sofia Ramos: are there any known gotchas for cross-account role setup? I've done lots of account-specific issues with policies.
[08:53] Priya Shah: yes, make sure the AWS roles assume permission and the KMS key policy includes the Redwood service principal. cross-account STS and proper trust relationships are essential. also, when using S3 endpoints ensure your bucket policy allows the service role and VPC endpoint principals. we'll provide sample CloudFormation/IaC snippets.
[09:15] Marcus Grant: regarding model updates — if a model is patched or replaced, do you do in-place updates or spin up new nodes? how does that affect connections?
[09:26] Priya Shah: we do rolling upgrades with canary traffic policies. for private deployments we can do canary traffic within your environment and fallback to previous model variants if regressions are detected. connections stay intact; we drain gracefully.
[09:43] Liam O'Hara: security review: do you have penetration test reports and third-party audits?
[09:48] Marta Nguyen: yes we have pentest summaries and third-party audit attestations; i'll include the SOC2 report and summary of pen test findings in the pack.
[09:58] Jared Lee: ok let's dig into a couple technical specifics — Ana, can you share how many accounts and VPCs you'd want connected?
[10:05] Ana Perez: currently 6 accounts, roughly 12 VPCs across prod/stage/dev. we'd prefer a central shared services VPC approach with transit gateway.
[10:15] Priya Shah: transit gateway is best for that — Redwood can peer into your shared services VPC or attach to your transit gateway. we just need the TGW attachment and route table entries. once attached we can present the service via PrivateLink into other accounts if you prefer not to modify many route tables.
[10:36] Marcus Grant: can you do mutual TLS for per-request authentication? we don't want tokens flying in plain, and we want short-lived credentials.
[10:45] Priya Shah: yes we support mTLS and short-lived tokens. we also have integration with Vault for short lived creds if you want dynamic secrets.
[10:56] Sofia Ramos: logging flow — we want request metadata (trace id, user id hash, latency) but not full prompt text in our logs. is that supported?
[11:04] Marta Nguyen: yes we can redact full prompt text and emit only hashed identifiers and metadata. we'll show the config during the deep dive.
[11:14] Jared Lee: quick note on quotas and throttles — in private/dedicated you get configurable throughput, hosted is subject to shared limits. we'll draft recommended capacity for the pilot.
[11:26] Marcus Grant: do you support private ECR/GCR for model images if we want to bring our own fine-tuned models?
[11:33] Priya Shah: yes, we can pull from private registries using cross-account roles or via a pull proxy in your VPC. for extra security we support signed images and scanning.
[11:44] Ana Perez: can we run in our air-gapped environment? we have a remote cluster that cannot reach the public cloud.
[11:51] Priya Shah: we have an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments with an offline installer and local control plane. that often requires a bit more ops support from engineering, but it's supported for high compliance customers.
[12:06] Liam O'Hara: network monitoring — we want VPC flow logs, and we want to ensure no unexpected egress. is there a recommended checklist?
[12:15] Priya Shah: yes we'll provide a network checklist: required security groups, NACLs, endpoint configs, required ports (mostly TCP 443 outbound to endpoints or control plane IPs), peering route entries, and recommended Flow Logs settings.
[12:30] Marcus Grant: what's the timeframe to get a pilot up if we decide today?
[12:34] Jared Lee: once we have your network diagram and keys, we can stand up a pilot in 2-3 weeks for a private deployment. Dedicated reserved capacity takes a bit longer if you need procurement — usually 3-6 weeks.
[12:46] Sofia Ramos: procurement — our legal will need a DPA and security addendum. is that standard?
[12:51] Marta Nguyen: yes we have a DPA template and can add a security addendum. we'll include those in the pack.
[12:58] Ana Perez: minor question — do you support IPv6 endpoints?
[13:03] Priya Shah: currently our PrivateLink and peering flows are IPv4-first; IPv6 support is on the roadmap depending on provider. we can discuss workarounds if IPv6 is a hard requirement.
[13:15] Marcus Grant: thanks — this is very helpful. any performance tuning suggestions for reducing token-costs?
[13:22] Jared Lee: a quick callout — batching, KV cache reuse, and quantized models all reduce cost. Redwood Optimize can analyze traces and recommend quantization/profile suggestions for your workload.
[13:36] Sofia Ramos: ok wrapping up — what do you need from us to move forward?
[13:41] Priya Shah: network diagram (VPCs, TGW, CIDRs), expected QPS and payload sizes, KMS key ARNs, and a list of accounts to attach.
[13:51] Ana Perez: we'll get that by next tuesday.
[13:54] Jared Lee: perfect. next steps recap: i'll send security pack and SOC2, priya will prepare VPC peering vs PrivateLink doc and IaC snippets, marta will share compliance artifacts, and we'll schedule a technical deep dive next week.
[14:10] Marcus Grant: great. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

References/Shared links mentioned: - SOC2 report (link to be shared) - VPC private endpoints comparison doc (to be shared) - IaC sample snippets (CloudFormation/Terraform) - Pilot TCO spreadsheet (pricing estimate)

Recap (auto): Redwood to provide security docs and network checklist; customer to provide network diagram, KMS ARNs and decide pilot scope.
